Facts necessary for the disposal of the Rule are as follows:-The opposite party No.2 obtained on 26-12-80 a decree for Tk. 13,414/50 with costs against opposite party Nos. 3 and 4 for arrears of rent in Money Suit No. 5 of 1977. Thereafter the decree-holder-opposite party No. 2 filed the aforesaid Money Execution Case No.4 of 1981 for realization of the decretal amount by attachment and sale of 4 items of machineries listed in execution petition as immovable properties under Rule 54 of order 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure. It has not however been stated in the application for execution whether the machineries are attached to the earth or not but it has been stated that the machineries are in the hut situated at the contiguous east of Nahagonj Oil Mill upon tiling of the aforesaid application for execution of the decree, sale proclamation under Rule 66 of order 21 C.P.C. was duly served as prayed For by the decree-holder fixing 11-9-81 for auction sale of the properties. In the auction the opposite party No.1 purchased the attached properties at the highest bid of Tk. 1,19,650/00 and on depositing the earnest money and subsequently the balance amount of the said bid, the sale was confirmed on 19-11-81. The decree-holder as well participated in the auction but failed to purchase the machineries. The decreetal amount with cost was credited to the satisfaction of the decree-holder and the balance of the sale proceeds were kept to the credit of the judgment-debtor i.e. the owners of the properties. 

 3. After confirmation of the sale the decree-holder opposite party No.2 filed an application under section 151 C.P.C. for setting aside the sale on the ground of irregularity in the matter of attachment of the property under order 21 Rule 54 C.P.C. but without pleading any sub-stantial injuries by reasons of such irregularity in the application. The learned Subordinate fudge, however, upon hearing the application set aside the auction sale and further directed the execution case should proceed in accordance with law. Against that order of the learned Subordinate Judge the auction purchaser opposite party No.1 moved this court in revision and obtained a Rule. It has been noticed at the time of the hearing of that Rule by their Lordships of this High Court Division that the decree-holder opposite party No.2 applied for execution of the decree by attachment of the properties which are Mill machineries under Rule 54 of Order 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In this application under section 151 C.P.C. for setting aside the sale the decree holder took the plea that the attachment of the properties under Rule 54 was irregular in that the rule related to immovable properties. It has been also noticed by their Lordships While hearing the rule that the objection as to alleged irregularity in the attachment of the properties was taken only when the decree-holder could not succeeded in the bid to purchase the machineries. It has also been noticed that no objection was taken by the decree-holder within 30 days from the date of the sale and the sale was accordingly confirmed. 

 11. As to the objection that the machineries being attached to the earth and as such being immovable properties under section 3 of the Transfer of Property Act read with section 3(25) of the General Clauses Act, the attachment and the sale of the machineries as movables are illegal and void, we are called upon to decide whether the machineries by the auction-purchaser arc immovable properties. The decree-holder-opposite party No. 2 was an ex-proprietor whose lands and premises in the Bazar as appears from the judgment in some First Appeals disposed of analogously, have vested in the Government as hat and bazars. The judgment-debtor-opposite party Nos. 3 and 4 as defendants in the Money Suit were tenants under the said landlord-decree-holder. The machineries of the aforesaid Gour Oil Mill belonged to the said tenant-judgment-debtor. The question is whether the machineries sold in auction in execution of the aforesaid Money decree and purchased by the auction-purchaser-opposite party No.1 who is a third party, are immovable properties. Judicial authorities have applied two tests to determine what is and what is not an immovable property as a result of attachment or annexation of the machineries to the land; that tests are:-(1) the degree or mode of annexation and (2) the object of annexation. Of the two tests the latter is more important and it is a question which depends upon the particular circumstances of each case. The test is the object with which the machinery is affixed. The machineries to attain the character of a permanent attachment so as to become an immovable property it must partake of the character of the attachment of trees and shrubs rooted to the earth or wall or holdings imbedded in the earth. The test is whether such attachment is for permanent beneficial enjoyment of the immovable properly to which it is attached.
